<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro primo Regum
<r>1 Reg 17:31-33</r>
<n>31</n> Audíta sunt autem verba, quæ locútus est David, et annuntiáta in conspéctu Saul.
<n>32</n> Ad quem cum fuísset addúctus, locútus est ei: Non cóncidat cor cuiúsquam in eo: ego servus tuus vadam et pugnábo advérsus Philisthǽum.
<n>33</n> Et ait Saul ad David: Non vales resistere Philisthǽo isti nec pugnáre advérsus eum, quia puer es, hic autem vir bellátor est ab adulescéntia sua.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Præparáte corda vestra Dómino, et servíte illi soli:
* Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.
<r>℣.</r> Convertímini ad eum in toto corde vestro, et auférte deos aliénos de médio vestri.
<r>℟.</r> Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the first book of Samuel
<r>1 Sam 17:31-33</r>
<n>31</n> And the words which David spoke were heard, and were rehearsed before Saul.
<n>32</n> And when he was brought to him, he said to him: Let not any man's heart be dismayed in him: I thy servant will go, and will fight against the Philistine.
<n>33</n> And Saul said to David: Thou art not able to withstand this Philistine, nor to fight against him: for thou art but a boy, but he is a warrior from his youth.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve Him Only
* And He will deliver you out of the hand of your enemies.
<r>℣.</r> Return unto Him with all your hearts, and put away the strange gods from among you.
<r>℟.</r> And He will deliver you out of the hand of your enemies.

<r>1 Reg 17:34-36</r>
<n>34</n> Dixítque David ad Saul: Pascébat servus tuus patris sui gregem, et veniébat leo vel ursus et tollébat aríetem de médio gregis,
<n>35</n> Et persequébar eos et percutiébam eruebámque de ore eórum; et illi consurgébant advérsum me, et apprehendébam mentum eórum et suffocábam interficiebámque eos;
<n>36</n> Nam et leónem et ursum interféci ego servus tuus.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Percússit Saul mille, et David decem míllia:
quia manus Dómini erat cum illo: percússit Philisthǽum,
* Et ábstulit oppróbrium ex Israël.
<r>℣.</r> Nonne iste est David, de quo canébant in choro, dicéntes: Saul percússit mille, et David decem míllia in míllibus suis?
<r>℟.</r> Et ábstulit oppróbrium ex Israël.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>1 Sam 17:34-36</r>
<n>34</n> And David said to Saul: thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, or a bear, and took a ram out of the midst of the flock:
<n>35</n> And I pursued after them, and struck them, and delivered it out of their mouth: and they rose up against me, and I caught them by the throat, and I strangled and killed them.
<n>36</n> For I thy servant have killed both a lion and a bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be also as one of them. I will go now, and take away the reproach of the people: for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, who hath dared to curse the army of the living God?
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.
because the hand of the Lord was with him, he smote the Philistine,
* And took away the reproach from Israel.
<r>℣.</r> Is not this David in míllibus suis? Did they not sing one to another of him in dances, saying: Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?
<r>℟.</r> And took away the reproach from Israel.

b.3f1a827d03:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui diligéntibus te bona invisibília præparásti: infúnde córdibus nostris tui amóris afféctum; ut te in ómnibus et super ómnia diligéntes, promissiónes tuas, quæ omne desidérium súperant, consequámur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.8b52f817cb:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who hast prepared for them that love thee such good things as pass man's understanding; pour into our hearts such love toward thee, that we, loving thee in all things and above all things, may obtain thy promises, which exceed all that we can desire.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.1974ac1e36:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>N</c>ono Kaléndas Iúlii Luna undevicésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>V</h>igília Nativitátis sancti Ioánnis Baptístæ.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Ioánnis Presbýteri, qui, sub Iuliáno Apóstata, via Salária véteri, ante simulácrum Solis decollátus est, et corpus eius a beáto Concórdio Presbýtero iuxta Mártyrum Concília sepúltum.
<h>I</h>tem Romæ sanctæ Agrippínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ sub Valeriáno Imperatóre martýrium consummávit. Ipsíus autem corpus, in Sicíliam translátum ac Menis cónditum, multis miráculis corúscat.
<h>S</h>útrii, in Túscia, sancti Felícis Presbýteri, cuius os támdiu iussit Túrcius Præféctus lápide contúndi, donec ipse Felix emítteret spíritum.
<h>N</h>icomedíæ commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, témpore Diocletiáni, in móntibus et spelúncis laténtes, pro Christi nómine martýrium læto ánimo subiérunt.
<h>P</h>hiladelphíæ, in Arábia, sanctórum Mártyrum Zenónis, eiúsque servi Zenæ. Hic dómini sui vincti caténas exósculans, eúmque rogans ut se in torméntis partícipem dignarétur habére, a milítibus tentus est, et cum ipso dómino parem martýrii corónam accépit.
<h>A</h>ugústæ Taurinórum sancti Ioséphi Cafásso, Sacerdótis, qui levítis pietáte et sciéntia augéndis atque damnátis cápite Deo conciliándis fuit illústris, et a Pio Papa Duodécimo inter sanctos Cǽlites adscríptus est.
<h>I</h>n monastério Elyénsi, in Británnia, sanctæ Ediltrúdis, Regínæ et Vírginis, quæ sanctitáte et miráculis clara migrávit ad Dóminum. Ipsíus autem corpus, úndecim post annis, invéntum est incorrúptum.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.a74596fd00:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>une 23rd 2027, the 19th day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>he morrow is the Eve of the holy Baptist John.
<h>U</h>pon the same 23rd day of June, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy Priest John, who was beheaded, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, in front of the image of the sun upon the old Salarian Way. His body was buried by the blessed Priest Concordius, hard by the martyrs' burial-place.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, under the Emperor Valerian, the holy Virgin and martyr Agrippina, whose body was taken to Sicily and is distinguished for many miracles.
<h>A</h>t Sutri, in Tuscany, the holy Priest Felix, whose mouth the Prefect Turcius ordered to be pounded with a stone until he died.
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia are commemorated very many holy martyrs who, in the time of Diocletian, wandered in deserts and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth, and for Christ's Name's sake, underwent martyrdom with joy.
<h>A</h>t Philadelphia, in Arabia, the holy martyr Zeno and Zenas his slave. When Zeno was bound Zenas kissed his chains, and besought him to be pleased to have him for a sharer in his torments, whereupon the soldiers took him, and he and his master received the same crown of martyrdom together, [in the year 304.]
<h>I</h>n England, the holy Queen and Virgin Etheldreda, who passed away to be with the Lord, illustrious for holiness and miracles whose body was found incorrupt eleven years after her death, [in the year 679.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
